1: The Python X Library
2: ====================
3: 
4: |Build Status| |codecov.io| |Code Health|
5: 
6: `Homepage`_ | `Releases`_ | `Changelog`_
7: 
8: Copyright
9: ~~~~~~~~~
10: 
11: The main part of the code is
12: 
13: ::
14: 
15:     Copyright (C) 2000-2002  Peter Liljenberg
16: 
17: Some contributed code is copyrighted by `the contributors <Contributors_>`_,
18: in these cases that is indicated in the source files in question.
19: 
20: The Python X Library is released under LGPL v2.1 or later (since 2016),
21: see the file LICENSE for details. 0.15rc1 and before were released under
22: GPL v2.
23: 
24: Requirements
25: ~~~~~~~~~~~~
26: 
27: The Python X Library requires Python 2.7 or newer. It has been tested to
28: various extents with Python 2.7 and 3.3 through 3.6.
29: 
30: The Python X Library will only work on systems that have an X server installed,
31: such as most Linux distros, but will not work on Windows or MacOS.
32: 
33: Installation
34: ~~~~~~~~~~~~
35: 
36: The Python Xlib uses the standard setuptools package, to install run
37: this command:
38: 
39: ::
40: 
41:     python setup.py install
42: 
43: See the command help for details: ``python setup.py install -h``.
44: 
45: Alternatively, you can run programs from the distribution directory, or
46: change the module path in programs.
47: 
48: There's a simple example program, implemented twice using both the
49: high-level interface and the low-level protocol.
50: 
51: Introduction
52: ~~~~~~~~~~~~
53: 
54: The Python X Library is intended to be a fully functional X client
55: library for Python programs. It is written entirely in Python, in
56: contrast to earlier X libraries for Python (the ancient X extension and
57: the newer plxlib) which were interfaces to the C Xlib.
58: 
59: This is possible to do since X client programs communicate with the X
60: server via the X protocol. The communication takes place over TCP/IP,
61: Unix sockets, DECnet or any other streaming network protocol. The C Xlib
62: is merely an interface to this protocol, providing functions suitable
63: for a C environment.
64: 
65: There are three advantages of implementing a pure Python library:
66: 
67: -  Integration: The library can make use of the wonderful object system
68:    in Python, providing an easy-to-use class hierarchy.
69: 
70: -  Portability: The library will be usable on (almost) any computer
71:    which have Python installed. A C interface could be problematic to
72:    port to non-Unix systems, such as MS Windows or OpenVMS.
73: 
74: -  Maintainability: It is much easier to develop and debug native Python
75:    modules than modules written in C.
76: 
77: Documentation
78: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~
79: 
80: The reference manual is not finished by far, but is probably still useful. It
81: can be `browsed online <https://python-xlib.github.io/>`__.
82: 
83: There are also some `example programs <Examples_>`_ and, of course,
84: `the standard X11 documentation <https://tronche.com/gui/x/xlib/>`__ applies.
85: 
86: 
87: Project status
88: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
89: 
90: The low-level protocol is complete, implementing client-side X11R6. The
91: high-level object oriented interface is also fully functional. It is
92: possible to write client applications with the library. Currently, the
93: only real application using Python Xlib is the window manager PLWM,
94: starting with version 2.0.
95: 
96: There is a resource database implementation, ICCCM support and a
97: framework for adding X extension code. Several extensions have been
98: implemented (RECORD, SHAPE, Xinerama, Composite, RANDR, DAMAGE,
99: Generic Event, SECURITY, XFIXES, XInput, XTEST, NV-CONTROL, DPMS and XRes);
100: patches for additions are very welcome.
101: 
102: There are most likely still bugs, but the library is at least stable
103: enough to run PLWM. A continuously bigger part of the library is covered
104: by regression tests, improving stability.
105: 
106: The documentation is still quite rudimentary, but should be of some help
107: for people programming with the Xlib. X beginners should first find some
108: general texts on X. A very good starting point is
109: http://www.rahul.net/kenton/xsites.html
110: 
111: See the file TODO for a detailed list of what is missing, approximately
112: ordered by importance.

145:         # Right, now we're all set up for the connection setup
146:         # request with the server.
147: 
148:         # Figure out which endianness the hardware uses
149:         self.big_endian = struct.unpack('BB', struct.pack('H', 0x0100))[0]
150: 
151:         if self.big_endian:
152:             order = 0x42
153:         else:
154:             order = 0x6c
155: 
156:         # Send connection setup
157:         r = ConnectionSetupRequest(self,
158:                                    byte_order = order,
159:                                    protocol_major = 11,
160:                                    protocol_minor = 0,
161:                                    auth_prot_name = auth_name,
162:                                    auth_prot_data = auth_data)
163: 
164:         # Did connection fail?
165:         if r.status != 1:
166:             raise error.DisplayConnectionError(self.display_name, r.reason)
167: 
168:         # Set up remaining info
169:         self.info = r
170:         self.default_screen = min(self.default_screen, len(self.info.roots) - 1)

187:     def next_event(self):
188:         self.check_for_error()
189: 
190:         # Main lock, so that only one thread at a time performs the
191:         # event waiting code.  This at least guarantees that the first
192:         # thread calling next_event() will get the next event, although
193:         # no order is guaranteed among other threads calling next_event()
194:         # while the first is blocking.
195: 
196:         self.event_queue_read_lock.acquire()
197: 
198:         # Lock event queue, so we can check if it is empty
199:         self.event_queue_write_lock.acquire()
200: 
201:         # We have too loop until we get an event, as
202:         # we might be woken up when there is no event.
203: 
204:         while not self.event_queue:
205: 
206:             # Lock send_recv so no send_and_receive
207:             # can start or stop while we're checking
208:             # whether there are one active.
209:             self.send_recv_lock.acquire()
210: 
211:             # Release event queue to allow an send_and_recv to
212:             # insert any now.
213:             self.event_queue_write_lock.release()
214: 
215:             # Call send_and_recv, which will return when
216:             # something has occured
217:             self.send_and_recv(event = True)
218: 
219:             # Before looping around, lock the event queue against
220:             # modifications.
221:             self.event_queue_write_lock.acquire()
222: 
223:         # Whiew, we have an event!  Remove it from
224:         # the event queue and relaese its write lock.
225: 
226:         event = self.event_queue[0]
227:         del self.event_queue[0]
228:         self.event_queue_write_lock.release()
229: 
230:         # Finally, allow any other threads which have called next_event()
231:         # while we were waiting to proceed.
232: 
233:         self.event_queue_read_lock.release()
234: 
235:         # And return the event!
236:         return event
237: 
238:     def pending_events(self):
239:         self.check_for_error()
240: 
241:         # Make a send_and_recv pass, receiving any events
242:         self.send_recv_lock.acquire()
243:         self.send_and_recv(recv = True)
244: 
245:         # Lock the queue, get the event count, and unlock again.
246:         self.event_queue_write_lock.acquire()
247:         count = len(self.event_queue)
248:         self.event_queue_write_lock.release()
249: 
250:         return count

265:     def allocate_resource_id(self):
266:         """id = d.allocate_resource_id()
267: 
268:         Allocate a new X resource id number ID.
269: 
270:         Raises ResourceIDError if there are no free resource ids.
271:         """
272: 
273:         self.resource_id_lock.acquire()
274:         try:
275:             i = self.last_resource_id
276:             while i in self.resource_ids:
277:                 i = i + 1
278:                 if i > self.info.resource_id_mask:
279:                     i = 0
280:                 if i == self.last_resource_id:
281:                     raise error.ResourceIDError('out of resource ids')
282: 
283:             self.resource_ids[i] = None
284:             self.last_resource_id = i
285:             return self.info.resource_id_base | i
286:         finally:
287:             self.resource_id_lock.release()

291:

293:         isn't allocated by us are ignored.

297:         try:
298:             i = rid & self.info.resource_id_mask
299: 
300:             # Attempting to free a resource id outside our range
301:             if rid - i != self.info.resource_id_base:
302:                 return None
303: 
304:             try:
305:                 del self.resource_ids[i]
306:             except KeyError:
307:                 pass
308:         finally:
309:             self.resource_id_lock.release()

387:     def send_and_recv(self, flush = False, event = False, request = None, recv = False):
388:         """send_and_recv(flush = None, event = None, request = None, recv = None)
389: 
390:         Perform I/O, or wait for some other thread to do it for us.
391: 
392:         send_recv_lock MUST be LOCKED when send_and_recv is called.
393:         It will be UNLOCKED at return.
394: 
395:         Exactly or one of the parameters flush, event, request and recv must
396:         be set to control the return condition.
397: 
398:         To attempt to send all requests in the queue, flush should
399:         be true.  Will return immediately if another thread is
400:         already doing send_and_recv.
401: 
402:         To wait for an event to be received, event should be true.
403: 
404:         To wait for a response to a certain request (either an error
405:         or a response), request should be set to that request's
406:         serial number.
407: 
408:         To just read any pending data from the server, recv should be true.
409: 
410:         It is not guaranteed that the return condition has been
411:         fulfilled when the function returns, so the caller has to loop
412:         until it is finished.
413:         """
414: 
415:         # We go to sleep if there is already a thread doing what we
416:         # want to do:
417: 
418:         #  If flushing, we want to send
419:         #  If waiting for a response to a request, we want to send
420:         #    (to ensure that the request was sent - we alway recv
421:         #     when we get to the main loop, but sending is the important
422:         #     thing here)
423:         #  If waiting for an event, we want to recv
424:         #  If just trying to receive anything we can, we want to recv
425: 
426:         # FIXME: It would be good if we could also sleep when we're waiting on
427:         # a response to a request that has already been sent.
428: 
429:         if (((flush or request is not None) and self.send_active)
430:             or ((event or recv) and self.recv_active)):
431: 
432:             # Signal that we are waiting for something.  These locks
433:             # together with the *_waiting variables are used as
434:             # semaphores.  When an event or a request response arrives,
435:             # it will zero the *_waiting and unlock the lock.  The
436:             # locks will also be unlocked when an active send_and_recv
437:             # finishes to signal the other waiting threads that one of
438:             # them has to take over the send_and_recv function.
439: 
440:             # All this makes these locks and variables a part of the
441:             # send_and_recv control logic, and hence must be modified
442:             # only when we have the send_recv_lock locked.
443:             if event:
444:                 wait_lock = self.event_wait_lock
445:                 if not self.event_waiting:
446:                     self.event_waiting = 1
447:                     wait_lock.acquire()
448: 
449:             elif request is not None:
450:                 wait_lock = self.request_wait_lock
451:                 if not self.request_waiting:
452:                     self.request_waiting = 1
453:                     wait_lock.acquire()
454: 
455:             # Release send_recv, allowing a send_and_recive
456:             # to terminate or other threads to queue up
457:             self.send_recv_lock.release()
458: 
459:             # Return immediately if flushing, even if that
460:             # might mean that not necessarily all requests
461:             # have been sent.
462:             if flush or recv:
463:                 return
464: 
465:             # Wait for something to happen, as the wait locks are
466:             # unlocked either when what we wait for has arrived (not
467:             # necessarily the exact object we're waiting for, though),
468:             # or when an active send_and_recv exits.
469: 
470:             # Release it immediately afterwards as we're only using
471:             # the lock for synchonization.  Since we're not modifying
472:             # event_waiting or request_waiting here we don't have
473:             # to lock send_and_recv_lock.  In fact, we can't do that
474:             # or we trigger a dead-lock.
475: 
476:             wait_lock.acquire()
477:             wait_lock.release()
478: 
479:             # Return to caller to let it check whether it has
480:             # got the data it was waiting for
481:             return
482: 
483: 
484:         # There's no thread doing what we need to do.  Find out exactly
485:         # what to do
486: 
487:         # There must always be some thread receiving data, but it must not
488:         # necessarily be us
489: 
490:         if not self.recv_active:
491:             receiving = 1
492:             self.recv_active = 1
493:         else:
494:             receiving = 0
495: 
496:         flush_bytes = None
497:         sending = 0
498: 
499:         # Loop, receiving and sending data.
500:         while 1:
501: 
502:             # We might want to start sending data
503:             if sending or not self.send_active:
504: 
505:                 # Turn all requests on request queue into binary form
506:                 # and append them to self.data_send
507: 
508:                 self.request_queue_lock.acquire()
509:                 for req, wait in self.request_queue:
510:                     self.data_send = self.data_send + req._binary
511:                     if wait:
512:                         self.sent_requests.append(req)
513: 
514:                 del self.request_queue[:]
515:                 self.request_queue_lock.release()
516: 
517:                 # If there now is data to send, mark us as senders
518: 
519:                 if self.data_send:
520:                     self.send_active = 1
521:                     sending = 1
522:                 else:
523:                     self.send_active = 0
524:                     sending = 0
525: 
526:             # We've done all setup, so release the lock and start waiting
527:             # for the network to fire up
528:             self.send_recv_lock.release()
529: 
530:             # There's no longer anything useful we can do here.
531:             if not (sending or receiving):
532:                 break
533: 
534:             # If we're flushing, figure out how many bytes we
535:             # have to send so that we're not caught in an interminable
536:             # loop if other threads continuously append requests.
537:             if flush and flush_bytes is None:
538:                 flush_bytes = self.data_sent_bytes + len(self.data_send)
539: 
540: 
541:             try:
542:                 # We're only checking for the socket to be writable
543:                 # if we're the sending thread.  We always check for it
544:                 # to become readable: either we are the receiving thread
545:                 # and should take care of the data, or the receiving thread
546:                 # might finish receiving after having read the data
547: 
548:                 if sending:
549:                     writeset = [self.socket]
550:                 else:
551:                     writeset = []
552: 
553:                 # Timeout immediately if we're only checking for
554:                 # something to read or if we're flushing, otherwise block
555: 
556:                 if recv or flush:
557:                     timeout = 0
558:                 else:
559:                     timeout = None
560: 
561:                 rs, ws, es = select.select([self.socket], writeset, [], timeout)
562: 
563:             # Ignore errors caused by a signal received while blocking.
564:             # All other errors are re-raised.
565:             except select.error as err:
566:                 if isinstance(err, OSError):
567:                     code = err.errno
568:                 else:
569:                     code = err[0]
570:                 if code != errno.EINTR:
571:                     raise
572: 
573:                 # We must lock send_and_recv before we can loop to
574:                 # the start of the loop
575: 
576:                 self.send_recv_lock.acquire()
577:                 continue
578: 
579: 
580:             # Socket is ready for sending data, send as much as possible.
581:             if ws:
582:                 try:
583:                     i = self.socket.send(self.data_send)
584:                 except socket.error as err:
585:                     self.close_internal('server: %s' % err)
586:                     raise self.socket_error
587: 
588:                 self.data_send = self.data_send[i:]
589:                 self.data_sent_bytes = self.data_sent_bytes + i
590: 
591: 
592:             # There is data to read
593:             gotreq = 0
594:             if rs:
595: 
596:                 # We're the receiving thread, parse the data
597:                 if receiving:
598:                     try:
599:                         count = self.recv_packet_len - len(self.data_recv)
600:                         count = max(self.recv_buffer_size, count)
601:                         bytes_recv = self.socket.recv(count)
602:                     except socket.error as err:
603:                         self.close_internal('server: %s' % err)
604:                         raise self.socket_error
605: 
606:                     if not bytes_recv:
607:                         # Clear up, set a connection closed indicator and raise it
608:                         self.close_internal('server')
609:                         raise self.socket_error
610: 
611:                     self.data_recv = bytes(self.data_recv) + bytes_recv
612:                     gotreq = self.parse_response(request)
613: 
614:                 # Otherwise return, allowing the calling thread to figure
615:                 # out if it has got the data it needs
616:                 else:
617:                     # We must be a sending thread if we're here, so reset
618:                     # that indicator.
619:                     self.send_recv_lock.acquire()
620:                     self.send_active = 0
621:                     self.send_recv_lock.release()
622: 
623:                     # And return to the caller
624:                     return
625: 
626: 
627:             # There are three different end of send-recv-loop conditions.
628:             # However, we don't leave the loop immediately, instead we
629:             # try to send and receive any data that might be left.  We
630:             # do this by giving a timeout of 0 to select to poll
631:             # the socket.
632: 
633:             # When flushing: all requests have been sent
634:             if flush and flush_bytes >= self.data_sent_bytes:
635:                 break
636: 
637:             # When waiting for an event: an event has been read
638:             if event and self.event_queue:
639:                 break
640: 
641:             # When processing a certain request: got its reply
642:             if request is not None and gotreq:
643:                 break
644: 
645:             # Always break if we just want to receive as much as possible
646:             if recv:
647:                 break
648: 
649:             # Else there's may still data which must be sent, or
650:             # we haven't got the data we waited for.  Lock and loop
651: 
652:             self.send_recv_lock.acquire()
653: 
654: 
655:         # We have accomplished the callers request.
656:         # Record that there are now no active send_and_recv,
657:         # and wake up all waiting thread
658: 
659:         self.send_recv_lock.acquire()
660: 
661:         if sending:
662:             self.send_active = 0
663:         if receiving:
664:             self.recv_active = 0
665: 
666:         if self.event_waiting:
667:             self.event_waiting = 0
668:             self.event_wait_lock.release()
669: 
670:         if self.request_waiting:
671:             self.request_waiting = 0
672:             self.request_wait_lock.release()
673: 
674:         self.send_recv_lock.release()
675:

677:     def parse_response(self, request):
678:         """Internal method.
679: 
680:         Parse data received from server.  If REQUEST is not None
681:         true is returned if the request with that serial number
682:         was received, otherwise false is returned.
683: 
684:         If REQUEST is -1, we're parsing the server connection setup
685:         response.
686:         """
687: 
688:         if request == -1:
689:             return self.parse_connection_setup()
690: 
691:         # Parse ordinary server response
692:         gotreq = False
693:         while True:
694:             if self.data_recv:
695:                 # Check the first byte to find out what kind of response it is
696:                 rtype = byte2int(self.data_recv)
697: 
698:             # Are we're waiting for additional data for the current packet?
699:             if self.recv_packet_len:
700:                 if len(self.data_recv) < self.recv_packet_len:
701:                     return gotreq
702: 
703:                 if rtype == 1:
704:                     gotreq = self.parse_request_response(request) or gotreq
705:                     continue
706:                 elif rtype & 0x7f == ge.GenericEventCode:
707:                     self.parse_event_response(rtype)
708:                     continue
709:                 else:
710:                     raise AssertionError(rtype)
711: 
712:             # Every response is at least 32 bytes long, so don't bother
713:             # until we have received that much
714:             if len(self.data_recv) < 32:
715:                 return gotreq
716: 
717:             # Error response
718:             if rtype == 0:
719:                 gotreq = self.parse_error_response(request) or gotreq
720: 
721:             # Request response or generic event.
722:             elif rtype == 1 or rtype & 0x7f == ge.GenericEventCode:
723:                 # Set reply length, and loop around to see if
724:                 # we have got the full response
725:                 rlen = int(struct.unpack('=L', self.data_recv[4:8])[0])
726:                 self.recv_packet_len = 32 + rlen * 4
727: 
728:             # Else non-generic event
729:             else:
730:                 self.parse_event_response(rtype)
731: 
732: 
733:     def parse_error_response(self, request):
734:         # Code is second byte
735:         code = indexbytes(self.data_recv, 1)
736: 
737:         # Fetch error class
738:         estruct = self.error_classes.get(code, error.XError)
739: 
740:         e = estruct(self, self.data_recv[:32])
741:         self.data_recv = bytesview(self.data_recv, 32)
742: 
743:         # print 'recv Error:', e
744: 
745:         req = self.get_waiting_request(e.sequence_number)
746: 
747:         # Error for a request whose response we are waiting for,
748:         # or which have an error handler.  However, if the error
749:         # handler indicates that it hasn't taken care of the
750:         # error, pass it on to the default error handler
751: 
752:         if req and req._set_error(e):
753: 
754:             # If this was a ReplyRequest, unlock any threads waiting
755:             # for a request to finish
756: 
757:             if isinstance(req, rq.ReplyRequest):
758:                 self.send_recv_lock.acquire()
759: 
760:                 if self.request_waiting:
761:                     self.request_waiting = 0
762:                     self.request_wait_lock.release()
763: 
764:                 self.send_recv_lock.release()
765: 
766:             return request == e.sequence_number
767: 
768:         # Else call the error handler
769:         else:
770:             if self.error_handler:
771:                 rq.call_error_handler(self.error_handler, e, None)
772:             else:
773:                 self.default_error_handler(e)
774: 
775:             return False
776: 
777: 
778:     def default_error_handler(self, err):
779:         sys.stderr.write('X protocol error:\n%s\n' % err)
780: 
781: 
782:     def parse_request_response(self, request):
783:         req = self.get_waiting_replyrequest()
784: 
785:         # Sequence number is always data[2:4]
786:         # Do sanity check before trying to parse the data
787:         sno = struct.unpack('=H', self.data_recv[2:4])[0]
788:         if sno != req._serial:
789:             raise RuntimeError("Expected reply for request %s, but got %s.  Can't happen!"
790:                                % (req._serial, sno))
791: 
792:         req._parse_response(self.data_recv[:self.recv_packet_len])
793:         # print 'recv Request:', req
794: 
795:         self.data_recv = bytesview(self.data_recv, self.recv_packet_len)
796:         self.recv_packet_len = 0
797: 
798: 
799:         # Unlock any response waiting threads
800: 
801:         self.send_recv_lock.acquire()
802: 
803:         if self.request_waiting:
804:             self.request_waiting = 0
805:             self.request_wait_lock.release()
806: 
807:         self.send_recv_lock.release()
808: 
809: 
810:         return req.sequence_number == request
811: 
812: 
813:     def parse_event_response(self, etype):
814:         # Skip bit 8, that is set if this event came from an SendEvent
815:         etype = etype & 0x7f
816: 
817:         if etype == ge.GenericEventCode:
818:             length = self.recv_packet_len
819:         else:
820:             length = 32
821: 
822:         estruct = self.event_classes.get(etype, event.AnyEvent)
823:         if type(estruct) == dict:
824:             subcode = self.data_recv[1]
825: 
826:             # Python2 compatibility
827:             if type(subcode) == str:
828:                 subcode = ord(subcode)
829: 
830:             # this etype refers to a set of sub-events with individual subcodes
831:             estruct = estruct[subcode]
832: 
833:         e = estruct(display = self, binarydata = self.data_recv[:length])
834: 
835:         if etype == ge.GenericEventCode:
836:             self.recv_packet_len = 0
837: 
838:         self.data_recv = bytesview(self.data_recv, length)
839: 
840:         # Drop all requests having an error handler,
841:         # but which obviously succeded.
842: 
843:         # Decrement it by one, so that we don't remove the request

34: class Xauthority(object):
35:     def __init__(self, filename = None):
36:         if filename is None:

38: 
39:         if filename is None:
40:             try:

52:         self.entries = []
53: 
54:         # entry format (all shorts in big-endian)
55:         #   short family;
56:         #   short addrlen;
57:         #   char addr[addrlen];
58:         #   short numlen;
59:         #   char num[numlen];
60:         #   short namelen;
61:         #   char name[namelen];
62:         #   short datalen;
63:         #   char data[datalen];
64: 
65:         n = 0
66:         try:
67:             while n < len(raw):

69:                 n = n + 2
70: 
71:                 length, = struct.unpack('>H', raw[n:n+2])
72:                 n = n + length + 2
73:                 addr = raw[n - length : n]
74: 
75:                 length, = struct.unpack('>H', raw[n:n+2])
76:                 n = n + length + 2
77:                 num = raw[n - length : n]
78: 
79:                 length, = struct.unpack('>H', raw[n:n+2])
80:                 n = n + length + 2
81:                 name = raw[n - length : n]
82: 
83:                 length, = struct.unpack('>H', raw[n:n+2])
84:                 n = n + length + 2
85:                 data = raw[n - length : n]
86: 
87:                 if len(data) != length:

89: 
90:                 self.entries.append((family, addr, num, name, data))

113: 
114:         If an entry is found, the tuple (name, data) is returned,
115:         otherwise XNoAuthError is raised.
116:         """

118:         num = str(dispno).encode()
119: 
120:         matches = {}
121: 
122:         for efam, eaddr, enum, ename, edata in self.entries:
123:             if enum == b'' and ename not in matches:
124:                 enum = num
125:             if efam == family and eaddr == address and num == enum:
126:                 matches[ename] = edata

128:         for t in types:
129:             try:

132:                 pass

34: # Set up a few regexpes for parsing string representation of resources
35: 
36: comment_re = re.compile(r'^\s*!')
37: resource_spec_re = re.compile(r'^\s*([-_a-zA-Z0-9?.*]+)\s*:\s*(.*)$')
38: value_escape_re = re.compile('\\\\([ \tn\\\\]|[0-7]{3,3})')
39: resource_parts_re = re.compile(r'([.*]+)')

41: # Constants used for determining which match is best
42: 
43: NAME_MATCH = 0
44: CLASS_MATCH = 2
45: WILD_MATCH = 4
46: MATCH_SKIP = 6

53: class ResourceDB(object):
54:     def __init__(self, file = None, string = None, resources = None):
55:         self.db = {}
56:         self.lock = lock.allocate_lock()
57: 
58:         if file is not None:
59:             self.insert_file(file)
60:         if string is not None:
61:             self.insert_string(string)
62:         if resources is not None:
63:             self.insert_resources(resources)

65:     def insert_file(self, file):
66:         """insert_file(file)
67: 
68:         Load resources entries from FILE, and insert them into the
69:         database.  FILE can be a filename (a string)or a file object.
70: 
71:         """
72: 
73:         if type(file) is bytes:
74:             file = open(file, 'r')
75: 
76:         self.insert_string(file.read())

79:     def insert_string(self, data):
80:         """insert_string(data)
81: 
82:         Insert the resources entries in the string DATA into the
83:         database.
84: 
85:         """
86: 
87:         # First split string into lines
88:         lines = data.split('\n')
89: 
90:         while lines:
91:             line = lines[0]
92:             del lines[0]
93: 
94:             # Skip empty line
95:             if not line:
96:                 continue
97: 
98:             # Skip comments
99:             if comment_re.match(line):
100:                 continue
101: 
102:             # Handle continued lines
103:             while line[-1] == '\\':
104:                 if lines:
105:                     line = line[:-1] + lines[0]
106:                     del lines[0]
107:                 else:
108:                     line = line[:-1]
109:                     break
110: 
111:             # Split line into resource and value
112:             m = resource_spec_re.match(line)
113: 
114:             # Bad line, just ignore it silently
115:             if not m:
116:                 continue
117: 
118:             res, value = m.group(1, 2)
119: 
120:             # Convert all escape sequences in value
121:             splits = value_escape_re.split(value)
122: 
123:             for i in range(1, len(splits), 2):
124:                 s = splits[i]
125:                 if len(s) == 3:
126:                     splits[i] = chr(int(s, 8))
127:                 elif s == 'n':
128:                     splits[i] = '\n'
129: 
130:             # strip the last value part to get rid of any
131:             # unescaped blanks
132:             splits[-1] = splits[-1].rstrip()
133: 
134:             value = ''.join(splits)
135: 
136:             self.insert(res, value)
137:

139:     def insert_resources(self, resources):
140:         """insert_resources(resources)
141: 
142:         Insert all resources entries in the list RESOURCES into the
143:         database.  Each element in RESOURCES should be a tuple:
144: 
145:           (resource, value)
146: 
147:         Where RESOURCE is a string and VALUE can be any Python value.
148: 
149:         """
150: 
151:         for res, value in resources:
152:             self.insert(res, value)
153: 
154:     def insert(self, resource, value):
155:         """insert(resource, value)
156: 
157:         Insert a resource entry into the database.  RESOURCE is a
158:         string and VALUE can be any Python value.
159: 
160:         """
161: 
162:         # Split res into components and bindings
163:         parts = resource_parts_re.split(resource)
164: 
165:         # If the last part is empty, this is an invalid resource
166:         # which we simply ignore
167:         if parts[-1] == '':
168:             return
169: 
170:         self.lock.acquire()
171: 
172:         db = self.db
173:         for i in range(1, len(parts), 2):
174: 
175:             # Create a new mapping/value group
176:             if parts[i - 1] not in db:
177:                 db[parts[i - 1]] = ({}, {})
178: 
179:             # Use second mapping if a loose binding, first otherwise
180:             if '*' in parts[i]:
181:                 db = db[parts[i - 1]][1]
182:             else:
183:                 db = db[parts[i - 1]][0]
184: 
185:         # Insert value into the derived db
186:         if parts[-1] in db:
187:             db[parts[-1]] = db[parts[-1]][:2] + (value, )
188:         else:
189:             db[parts[-1]] = ({}, {}, value)
190: 
191:         self.lock.release()

193:     def __getitem__(self, keys_tuple):
194:         """db[name, class]
195: 
196:         Return the value matching the resource identified by NAME and
197:         CLASS.  If no match is found, KeyError is raised.
198:         """
199: 
200:         # Split name and class into their parts
201:         name, cls = keys_tuple
202: 
203:         namep = name.split('.')
204:         clsp = cls.split('.')
205: 
206:         # It is an error for name and class to have different number
207:         # of parts
208: 
209:         if len(namep) != len(clsp):
210:             raise ValueError('Different number of parts in resource name/class: %s/%s' % (name, cls))
211: 
212:         complen = len(namep)
213:         matches = []
214: 
215:         # Lock database and wrap the lookup code in a try-finally
216:         # block to make sure that it is unlocked.
217: 
218:         self.lock.acquire()
219:         try:
220: 
221:             # Precedence order: name -> class -> ?
222: 
223:             if namep[0] in self.db:
224:                 bin_insert(matches, _Match((NAME_MATCH, ), self.db[namep[0]]))
225: 
226:             if clsp[0] in self.db:
227:                 bin_insert(matches, _Match((CLASS_MATCH, ), self.db[clsp[0]]))
228: 
229:             if '?' in self.db:
230:                 bin_insert(matches, _Match((WILD_MATCH, ), self.db['?']))
231: 
232: 
233:             # Special case for the unlikely event that the resource
234:             # only has one component
235:             if complen == 1 and matches:
236:                 x = matches[0]
237:                 if x.final(complen):
238:                     return x.value()
239:                 else:
240:                     raise KeyError((name, cls))
241: 
242: 
243:             # Special case for resources which begins with a loose
244:             # binding, e.g. '*foo.bar'
245:             if '' in self.db:
246:                 bin_insert(matches, _Match((), self.db[''][1]))
247: 
248: 
249:             # Now iterate over all components until we find the best match.
250: 
251:             # For each component, we choose the best partial match among
252:             # the mappings by applying these rules in order:
253: 
254:             # Rule 1: If the current group contains a match for the
255:             # name, class or '?', we drop all previously found loose
256:             # binding mappings.
257: 
258:             # Rule 2: A matching name has precedence over a matching
259:             # class, which in turn has precedence over '?'.
260: 
261:             # Rule 3: Tight bindings have precedence over loose
262:             # bindings.
263: 
264:             while matches:
265: 
266:                 # Work on the first element == the best current match
267: 
268:                 x = matches[0]
269:                 del matches[0]
270: 
271:                 # print 'path:  ', x.path
272:                 # if x.skip:
273:                 #         print 'skip:  ', x.db
274:                 # else:
275:                 #         print 'group: ', x.group
276:                 # print
277: 
278:                 i = x.match_length()
279: 
280:                 for part, score in ((namep[i], NAME_MATCH),
281:                                     (clsp[i], CLASS_MATCH),
282:                                     ('?', WILD_MATCH)):
283: 
284:                     # Attempt to find a match in x
285:                     match = x.match(part, score)
286:                     if match:
287:                         # Hey, we actually found a value!
288:                         if match.final(complen):
289:                             return match.value()
290: 
291:                         # Else just insert the new match
292:                         else:
293:                             bin_insert(matches, match)
294: 
295:                     # Generate a new loose match
296:                     match = x.skip_match(complen)
297:                     if match:
298:                         bin_insert(matches, match)
299: 
300:             # Oh well, nothing matched
301:             raise KeyError((name, cls))
302: 
303:         finally:
304:             self.lock.release()
305: 
306:     def get(self, res, cls, default = None):
307:         """get(name, class [, default])
308: 
309:         Return the value matching the resource identified by NAME and
310:         CLASS.  If no match is found, DEFAULT is returned, or None if
311:         DEFAULT isn't specified.
312: 
313:         """
314: 
315:         try:
316:             return self[(res, cls)]
317:         except KeyError:
318:             return default

320:     def update(self, db):
321:         """update(db)
322: 
323:         Update this database with all resources entries in the resource
324:         database DB.
325: 
326:         """
327: 
328:         self.lock.acquire()
329:         update_db(self.db, db.db)
330:         self.lock.release()
331: 
332:     def output(self):
333:         """output()
334: 
335:         Return the resource database in text representation.
336:         """
337: 
338:         self.lock.acquire()
339:         text = output_db('', self.db)
340:         self.lock.release()
341:         return text

343:     def getopt(self, name, argv, opts):
344:         """getopt(name, argv, opts)
345: 
346:         Parse X command line options, inserting the recognised options
347:         into the resource database.
348: 
349:         NAME is the application name, and will be prepended to all
350:         specifiers.  ARGV is the list of command line arguments,
351:         typically sys.argv[1:].
352: 
353:         OPTS is a mapping of options to resource specifiers.  The key is
354:         the option flag (with leading -), and the value is an instance of
355:         some Option subclass:
356: 
357:         NoArg(specifier, value): set resource to value.
358:         IsArg(specifier):        set resource to option itself
359:         SepArg(specifier):       value is next argument
360:         ResArg:                  resource and value in next argument
361:         SkipArg:                 ignore this option and next argument
362:         SkipLine:                ignore rest of arguments
363:         SkipNArgs(count):        ignore this option and count arguments
364: 
365:         The remaining, non-option, oparguments is returned.
366: 
367:         rdb.OptionError is raised if there is an error in the argument list.
368:         """
369: 
370:         while argv and argv[0] and argv[0][0] == '-':
371:             try:
372:                 argv = opts[argv[0]].parse(name, self, argv)
373:             except KeyError:
374:                 raise OptionError('unknown option: %s' % argv[0])
375:             except IndexError:
376:                 raise OptionError('missing argument to option: %s' % argv[0])
377: 
378:         return argv

381: class _Match(object):
382:     def __init__(self, path, dbs):
383:         self.path = path
384: 
385:         if type(dbs) is tuple:
386:             self.skip = 0
387:             self.group = dbs
388: 
389:         else:
390:             self.skip = 1
391:             self.db = dbs
392: 
393:     def __lt__(self, other):
394:         return self.path < other.path
395: 
396:     def __gt__(self, other):
397:         return self.path > other.path
398: 
399:     def __eq__(self, other):
400:         return self.path == other.path
401: 
402:     def match_length(self):
403:         return len(self.path)
404: 
405:     def match(self, part, score):
406:         if self.skip:
407:             if part in self.db:
408:                 return _Match(self.path + (score, ), self.db[part])
409:             else:
410:                 return None
411:         else:
412:             if part in self.group[0]:
413:                 return _Match(self.path + (score, ), self.group[0][part])
414:             elif part in self.group[1]:
415:                 return _Match(self.path + (score + 1, ), self.group[1][part])
416:             else:
417:                 return None
418: 
419:     def skip_match(self, complen):
420:         # Can't make another skip if we have run out of components
421:         if len(self.path) + 1 >= complen:
422:             return None
423: 
424:         # If this already is a skip match, clone a new one
425:         if self.skip:
426:             if self.db:
427:                 return _Match(self.path + (MATCH_SKIP, ), self.db)
428:             else:
429:                 return None
430: 
431:         # Only generate a skip match if the loose binding mapping
432:         # is non-empty
433:         elif self.group[1]:
434:             return _Match(self.path + (MATCH_SKIP, ), self.group[1])
435: 
436:         # This is a dead end match
437:         else:
438:             return None
439: 
440:     def final(self, complen):
441:         if not self.skip and len(self.path) == complen and len(self.group) > 2:
442:             return 1
443:         else:
444:             return 0
445: 
446:     def value(self):
447:         return self.group[2]

454: def bin_insert(list, element):
455:     """bin_insert(list, element)
456: 
457:     Insert ELEMENT into LIST.  LIST must be sorted, and ELEMENT will
458:     be inserted to that LIST remains sorted.  If LIST already contains
459:     ELEMENT, it will not be duplicated.
460: 
461:     """
462: 
463:     if not list:
464:         list.append(element)
465:         return
466: 
467:     lower = 0
468:     upper = len(list) - 1
469: 
470:     while lower <= upper:
471:         center = (lower + upper) // 2
472:         if element < list[center]:
473:             upper = center - 1
474:         elif element > list[center]:
475:             lower = center + 1
476:         elif element == list[center]:
477:             return
478: 
479:     if element < list[upper]:
480:         list.insert(upper, element)
481:     elif element > list[upper]:
482:         list.insert(upper + 1, element)

486: # Helper functions for ResourceDB.update()
487: #
488: 
489: def update_db(dest, src):
490:     for comp, group in src.items():
491: 
492:         # DEST already contains this component, update it
493:         if comp in dest:
494: 
495:             # Update tight and loose binding databases
496:             update_db(dest[comp][0], group[0])
497:             update_db(dest[comp][1], group[1])
498: 
499:             # If a value has been set in SRC, update
500:             # value in DEST
501: 
502:             if len(group) > 2:
503:                 dest[comp] = dest[comp][:2] + group[2:]
504: 
505:         # COMP not in src, make a deep copy
506:         else:
507:             dest[comp] = copy_group(group)
508: 
509: def copy_group(group):
510:     return (copy_db(group[0]), copy_db(group[1])) + group[2:]
511: 
512: def copy_db(db):
513:     newdb = {}
514:     for comp, group in db.items():
515:         newdb[comp] = copy_group(group)
516: 
517:     return newdb

520: #
521: # Helper functions for output
522: #
523: 
524: def output_db(prefix, db):
525:     res = ''
526:     for comp, group in db.items():
527: 
528:         # There's a value for this component
529:         if len(group) > 2:
530:             res = res + '%s%s: %s\n' % (prefix, comp, output_escape(group[2]))
531: 
532:         # Output tight and loose bindings
533:         res = res + output_db(prefix + comp + '.', group[0])
534:         res = res + output_db(prefix + comp + '*', group[1])
535: 
536:     return res

538: def output_escape(value):
539:     value = str(value)
540:     if not value:
541:         return value
542: 
543:     for char, esc in (('\\', '\\\\'),
544:                       ('\000', '\\000'),
545:                       ('\n', '\\n')):
546: 
547:         value = value.replace(char, esc)
548: 
549:     # If first or last character is space or tab, escape them.
550:     if value[0] in ' \t':
551:         value = '\\' + value
552:     if value[-1] in ' \t' and value[-2:-1] != '\\':
553:         value = value[:-1] + '\\' + value[-1]
554: 
555:     return value

559: # Option type definitions
560: #
561: 
562: class Option(object):
563:     def __init__(self):
564:         pass
565: 
566:     def parse(self, name, db, args):
567:         pass

569: class NoArg(Option):
570:     """Value is provided to constructor."""
571:     def __init__(self, specifier, value):
572:         self.specifier = specifier
573:         self.value = value
574: 
575:     def parse(self, name, db, args):
576:         db.insert(name + self.specifier, self.value)

579: class IsArg(Option):
580:     """Value is the option string itself."""
581:     def __init__(self, specifier):
582:         self.specifier = specifier
583: 
584:     def parse(self, name, db, args):

589:     """Value is the next argument."""
590:     def __init__(self, specifier):
591:         self.specifier = specifier
592: 
593:     def parse(self, name, db, args):
594:         db.insert(name + self.specifier, args[1])

599:     def parse(self, name, db, args):

629: def get_display_opts(options, argv = sys.argv):
630:     """display, name, db, args = get_display_opts(options, [argv])
631: 
632:     Parse X OPTIONS from ARGV (or sys.argv if not provided).
633: 
634:     Connect to the display specified by a *.display resource if one is
635:     set, or to the default X display otherwise.  Extract the
636:     RESOURCE_MANAGER property and insert all resources from ARGV.
637: 
638:     The four return values are:
639:       DISPLAY -- the display object
640:       NAME    -- the application name (the filname of ARGV[0])
641:       DB      -- the created resource database
642:       ARGS    -- any remaining arguments
643:     """

645:     from Xlib import display, Xatom

648:     name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(argv[0]))[0]
649: 
650:     optdb = ResourceDB()
651:     leftargv = optdb.getopt(name, argv[1:], options)

653:     dname = optdb.get(name + '.display', name + '.Display', None)
654:     d = display.Display(dname)

656:     rdbstring = d.screen(0).root.get_full_property(Xatom.RESOURCE_MANAGER,
657:                                                    Xatom.STRING)

685: # Notes on the implementation:
686: 
687: # Resource names are split into their components, and each component
688: # is stored in a mapping.  The value for a component is a tuple of two
689: # or three elements:
690: 
691: #   (tightmapping, loosemapping [, value])
692: 
693: # tightmapping contains the next components which are connected with a
694: # tight binding (.).  loosemapping contains the ones connected with
695: # loose binding (*).  If value is present, then this component is the
696: # last component for some resource which that value.
697: 
698: # The top level components are stored in the mapping r.db, where r is
699: # the resource object.
700: 
701: # Example:  Inserting "foo.bar*gazonk: yep" into an otherwise empty
702: # resource database would give the following structure:
703: 
704: # { 'foo': ( { 'bar': ( { },
705: #                       { 'gazonk': ( { },
706: #                                     { },
707: #                                     'yep')
708: #                         }
709: #                       )
710: #              },

64: class _BaseDisplay(protocol_display.Display):
65: 
66:     # Implement a cache of atom names, used by Window objects when
67:     # dealing with some ICCCM properties not defined in Xlib.Xatom
68: 
69:     def __init__(self, *args, **keys):
70:         self.resource_classes = _resource_baseclasses.copy()
71:         protocol_display.Display.__init__(self, *args, **keys)
72:         self._atom_cache = {}
73: 
74:     def get_atom(self, atomname, only_if_exists=False):
75:         if atomname in self._atom_cache:
76:             return self._atom_cache[atomname]
77: 
78:         r = request.InternAtom(display = self, name = atomname, only_if_exists = only_if_exists)
79: 
80:          # don't cache NONE responses in case someone creates this later
81:         if r.atom != X.NONE:
82:             self._atom_cache[atomname] = r.atom
83: 
84:         return r.atom
85:

87: class Display(object):
88:     def __init__(self, display = None):
89:         self.display = _BaseDisplay(display)
90: 
91:         # Create the keymap cache
92:         self._keymap_codes = [()] * 256
93:         self._keymap_syms = {}
94:         self._update_keymap(self.display.info.min_keycode,
95:                             (self.display.info.max_keycode
96:                              - self.display.info.min_keycode + 1))
97: 
98:         # Translations for keysyms to strings.
99:         self.keysym_translations = {}
100: 
101:         # Find all supported extensions
102:         self.extensions = []
103:         self.class_extension_dicts = {}
104:         self.display_extension_methods = {}
105: 
106:         # a dict that maps the event name to the code
107:         # or, when it's an event with a subcode, to a tuple of (event,subcode)
108:         # note this wraps the dict so you address it as
109:         # extension_event.EXTENSION_EVENT_NAME rather than
110:         # extension_event["EXTENSION_EVENT_NAME"]
111:         self.extension_event = rq.DictWrapper({})
112: 
113:         exts = self.list_extensions()
114: 
115:         # Go through all extension modules
116:         for extname, modname in ext.__extensions__:
117:             if extname in exts:
118: 
119:                 # Import the module and fetch it
120:                 __import__('Xlib.ext.' + modname)
121:                 mod = getattr(ext, modname)
122: 
123:                 info = self.query_extension(extname)
124:                 self.display.set_extension_major(extname, info.major_opcode)
125: 
126:                 # Call initialiasation function
127:                 mod.init(self, info)
128: 
129:                 self.extensions.append(extname)
130: 
131: 
132:         # Finalize extensions by creating new classes
133:         for class_name, dictionary in self.class_extension_dicts.items():
134:             origcls = self.display.resource_classes[class_name]
135:             self.display.resource_classes[class_name] = type(origcls.__name__,
136:                                                              (origcls,),
137:                                                              dictionary)
138: 
139:         # Problem: we have already created some objects without the
140:         # extensions: the screen roots and default colormaps.
141:         # Fix that by reinstantiating them.
142:         for screen in self.display.info.roots:
143:             screen.root = self.display.resource_classes['window'](self.display, screen.root.id)
144:             screen.default_colormap = self.display.resource_classes['colormap'](self.display, screen.default_colormap.id)

252:     def extension_add_method(self, object, name, function):
253:         """extension_add_method(object, name, function)
254: 
255:         Add an X extension module method.  OBJECT is the type of
256:         object to add the function to, a string from this list:
257: 
258:             display
259:             resource
260:             drawable
261:             window
262:             pixmap
263:             fontable
264:             font
265:             gc
266:             colormap
267:             cursor
268: 
269:         NAME is the name of the method, a string.  FUNCTION is a
270:         normal function whose first argument is a 'self'.
271:         """
272: 
273:         if object == 'display':
274:             if hasattr(self, name):
275:                 raise AssertionError('attempting to replace display method: %s' % name)
276: 
277:             self.display_extension_methods[name] = function
278: 
279:         else:
280:             class_list = (object, ) + _resource_hierarchy.get(object, ())
281:             for class_name in class_list:
282:                 cls = _resource_baseclasses[class_name]
283:                 if hasattr(cls, name):
284:                     raise AssertionError('attempting to replace %s method: %s' % (class_name, name))
285: 
286:                 method = create_unbound_method(function, cls)
287: 
288:                 # Maybe should check extension overrides too
289:                 try:
290:                     self.class_extension_dicts[class_name][name] = method
291:                 except KeyError:
292:                     self.class_extension_dicts[class_name] = { name: method }
293: 
294:     def extension_add_event(self, code, evt, name = None):
295:         """extension_add_event(code, evt, [name])
296: 
297:         Add an extension event.  CODE is the numeric code, and EVT is
298:         the event class.  EVT will be cloned, and the attribute _code
299:         of the new event class will be set to CODE.
300: 
301:         If NAME is omitted, it will be set to the name of EVT.  This
302:         name is used to insert an entry in the DictWrapper
303:         extension_event.
304:         """
305: 
306:         newevt = type(evt.__name__, evt.__bases__,
307:                       evt.__dict__.copy())
308:         newevt._code = code
309: 
310:         self.display.add_extension_event(code, newevt)
311: 
312:         if name is None:
313:             name = evt.__name__
314: 
315:         setattr(self.extension_event, name, code)
316: 
317:     def extension_add_subevent(self, code, subcode, evt, name = None):
318:         """extension_add_subevent(code, evt, [name])
319: 
320:         Add an extension subevent.  CODE is the numeric code, subcode
321:         is the sub-ID of this event that shares the code ID with other
322:         sub-events and EVT is the event class.  EVT will be cloned, and
323:         the attribute _code of the new event class will be set to CODE.
324: 
325:         If NAME is omitted, it will be set to the name of EVT.  This
326:         name is used to insert an entry in the DictWrapper
327:         extension_event.
328:         """
329: 
330:         newevt = type(evt.__name__, evt.__bases__,
331:                       evt.__dict__.copy())
332:         newevt._code = code
333: 
334:         self.display.add_extension_event(code, newevt, subcode)
335: 
336:         if name is None:
337:             name = evt.__name__
338: 
339:         # store subcodes as a tuple of (event code, subcode) in the
340:         # extension dict maintained in the display object
341:         setattr(self.extension_event, name, (code,subcode))
342: 
343:     def extension_add_error(self, code, err):
344:         """extension_add_error(code, err)
345: 
346:         Add an extension error.  CODE is the numeric code, and ERR is
347:         the error class.
348:         """
349: 
350:         self.display.add_extension_error(code, err)

352:     ###
353:     ### keymap cache implementation
354:     ###
355: 
356:     # The keycode->keysym map is stored in a list with 256 elements.
357:     # Each element represents a keycode, and the tuple elements are
358:     # the keysyms bound to the key.
359: 
360:     # The keysym->keycode map is stored in a mapping, where the keys
361:     # are keysyms.  The values are a sorted list of tuples with two
362:     # elements each: (index, keycode)
363:     # keycode is the code for a key to which this keysym is bound, and
364:     # index is the keysyms index in the map for that keycode.
365: 
366:     def keycode_to_keysym(self, keycode, index):
367:         """Convert a keycode to a keysym, looking in entry index.
368:         Normally index 0 is unshifted, 1 is shifted, 2 is alt grid, and 3
369:         is shift+alt grid. If that key entry is not bound, X.NoSymbol is
370:         returned."""
371:         try:
372:             return self._keymap_codes[keycode][index]
373:         except IndexError:
374:             return X.NoSymbol
375: 
376:     def keysym_to_keycode(self, keysym):
377:         """Look up the primary keycode that is bound to keysym. If
378:         several keycodes are found, the one with the lowest index and
379:         lowest code is returned. If keysym is not bound to any key, 0 is
380:         returned."""
381:         try:
382:             return self._keymap_syms[keysym][0][1]
383:         except (KeyError, IndexError):
384:             return 0
385: 
386:     def keysym_to_keycodes(self, keysym):
387:         """Look up all the keycodes that is bound to keysym. A list of
388:         tuples (keycode, index) is returned, sorted primarily on the
389:         lowest index and secondarily on the lowest keycode."""
390:         try:
391:             # Copy the map list, reversing the arguments
392:             return map(lambda x: (x[1], x[0]), self._keymap_syms[keysym])
393:         except KeyError:
394:             return []
395: 
396:     def refresh_keyboard_mapping(self, evt):
397:         """This method should be called once when a MappingNotify event
398:         is received, to update the keymap cache. evt should be the event
399:         object."""
400:         if isinstance(evt, event.MappingNotify):
401:             if evt.request == X.MappingKeyboard:
402:                 self._update_keymap(evt.first_keycode, evt.count)
403:         else:
404:             raise TypeError('expected a MappingNotify event')
405: 
406:     def _update_keymap(self, first_keycode, count):
407:         """Internal function, called to refresh the keymap cache.
408:         """
409: 
410:         # Delete all sym->code maps for the changed codes
411: 
412:         lastcode = first_keycode + count
413:         for keysym, codes in self._keymap_syms.items():
414:             i = 0
415:             while i < len(codes):
416:                 code = codes[i][1]
417:                 if code >= first_keycode and code < lastcode:
418:                     del codes[i]
419:                 else:
420:                     i = i + 1
421: 
422:         # Get the new keyboard mapping
423:         keysyms = self.get_keyboard_mapping(first_keycode, count)
424: 
425:         # Replace code->sym map with the new map
426:         self._keymap_codes[first_keycode:lastcode] = keysyms
427: 
428:         # Update sym->code map
429:         code = first_keycode
430:         for syms in keysyms:
431:             index = 0
432:             for sym in syms:
433:                 if sym != X.NoSymbol:
434:                     if sym in self._keymap_syms:
435:                         symcodes = self._keymap_syms[sym]
436:                         symcodes.append((index, code))
437:                         symcodes.sort()
438:                     else:
439:                         self._keymap_syms[sym] = [(index, code)]
440: 
441:                 index = index + 1
442:             code = code + 1
443: 
444:     ###
445:     ### client-internal keysym to string translations
446:     ###

448:     def lookup_string(self, keysym):
449:         """Return a string corresponding to KEYSYM, or None if no
450:         reasonable translation is found.
451:         """
452:         s = self.keysym_translations.get(keysym)
453:         if s is not None:
454:             return s
455: 
456:         import Xlib.XK
457:         return Xlib.XK.keysym_to_string(keysym)
458: 
459:     def rebind_string(self, keysym, newstring):
460:         """Change the translation of KEYSYM to NEWSTRING.
461:         If NEWSTRING is None, remove old translation if any.
462:         """
463:         if newstring is None:
464:             try:
465:                 del self.keysym_translations[keysym]
466:             except KeyError:
467:                 pass
468:         else:
469:             self.keysym_translations[keysym] = newstring

609:     def query_keymap(self):
610:         """Return a bit vector for the logical state of the keyboard,
611:         where each bit set to 1 indicates that the corresponding key is
612:         currently pressed down. The vector is represented as a list of 32
613:         integers. List item N contains the bits for keys 8N to 8N + 7
614:         with the least significant bit in the byte representing key 8N."""
615:         r = request.QueryKeymap(display = self.display)
616:         return r.map

618:     def open_font(self, name):
619:         """Open the font identifed by the pattern name and return its
620:         font object. If name does not match any font, None is returned."""
621:         fid = self.display.allocate_resource_id()
622:         ec = error.CatchError(error.BadName)
623: 
624:         request.OpenFont(display = self.display,
625:                          onerror = ec,
626:                          fid = fid,
627:                          name = name)
628:         self.sync()
629: 
630:         if ec.get_error():
631:             self.display.free_resource_id(fid)
632:             return None
633:         else:
634:             cls = self.display.get_resource_class('font', fontable.Font)
635:             return cls(self.display, fid, owner = 1)

637:     def list_fonts(self, pattern, max_names):
638:         """Return a list of font names matching pattern. No more than
639:         max_names will be returned."""
640:         r = request.ListFonts(display = self.display,
641:                               max_names = max_names,
642:                               pattern = pattern)
